function.name: task
function.description:
Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

description.description: A short (5-6 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The complete, autonomous brief for the agent to perform.

subagent_type.description: Which agent type to use: explore, implement, verify, web, pr.

task_id.description: Only to resume: the id from a previous task result — continues that agent with its context. Omit to start fresh.

function.name: task
function.description:
Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree
- mon-agent: custom agent

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree
- mon-agent: custom agent

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

description.description: A short (5-6 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The complete, autonomous brief for the agent to perform.

subagent_type.description: Which agent type to use: explore, implement, verify, web, pr, mon-agent.

task_id.description: Only to resume: the id from a previous task result — continues that agent with its context. Omit to start fresh.

Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

description.description: A short (5-6 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The complete, autonomous brief for the agent to perform.

subagent_type.description: Which agent type to use: explore, implement, verify, web, pr.

task_id.description: Only to resume: the id from a previous task result — continues that agent with its context. Omit to start fresh.

function.name: task
function.description:
Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree
- mon-agent: custom agent

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

function.name: task
function.description:
Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

function.description:
Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree
- ab_cd: custom agent
- revue: dddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddddd

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

task_id.description: Only to resume: the id from a previous task result — continues that agent with its context. Omit to start fresh.

Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

description.description: A short (5-6 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The complete, autonomous brief for the agent to perform.

subagent_type.description: Which agent type to use: explore, implement, verify, web, pr.

task_id.description: Only to resume: the id from a previous task result — continues that agent with its context. Omit to start fresh.

Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: branches, commits and opens the pull request for work already in the tree

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

description.description: A short (5-6 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The complete, autonomous brief for the agent to perform.

subagent_type.description: Which agent type to use: implement, verify, web, pr.

task_id.description: Only to resume: the id from a previous task result — continues that agent with its context. Omit to start fresh.

Launch an ephemeral sub-agent to handle a well-scoped sub-mission autonomously and report back. The agent runs its OWN tool loop in an isolated context (on the same model) and returns a single final report; its intermediate steps stay out of this conversation.

Available agent types (subagent_type):
- explore: read-only codebase exploration — locate code, read it, judge it, git history
- implement: writes the code change in the sandbox and verifies it (does not commit)
- verify: runs tests and commands, diagnoses failures, changes nothing
- web: web research specialist driving a real browser (pw_* tools)
- pr: une description
- revue: custom agent

Usage notes:
1. Fresh context by default: without task_id the agent starts blank, so the prompt MUST be a complete, autonomous brief — include all needed context and state EXPLICITLY what the final report must contain (paths, line numbers, quotes, links, values).
2. The result carries an id: pass it back as task_id to CONTINUE the same agent with its previous context (follow-up questions, refinements). This also works after a timeout/failure/cancellation when the error envelope carries a task_id — the agent resumes from its partial work. Best effort — if it expired, you get an error and should start fresh.
3. The agent's work is NOT shown to the user: always restate the result in your own answer.
4. When NOT to use: reading one known file (read it directly), a trivial 1-2 call lookup, or anything needing user interaction mid-task.
5. You may request several independent tasks in one message; they run one after another.

description.description: A short (5-6 word) description of the task.

prompt.description: The complete, autonomous brief for the agent to perform.

subagent_type.description: Which agent type to use: explore, implement, verify, web, pr, revue.

task_id.description: Only to resume: the id from a previous task result — continues that agent with its context. Omit to start fresh.
